claim: JWT date fields are plain numbers: seconds since the Unix epoch, not formatted date strings.
quote: A JSON numeric value representing the number of seconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC until the specified UTC date/time, ignoring leap seconds.

claim: If a validator does not find itself in a token's audience list, it has to reject the token.
quote: If the principal processing the claim does not identify itself with a value in the "aud" claim when this claim is present, then the JWT MUST be rejected.

claim: Tokens that fail signature validation have to be logged and reported back to the issuer.
quote: JWTs that fail signature validation MUST be logged and reported to the issuer.

claim: Expiration checks are allowed a little clock-skew leeway, on the order of a few minutes.
quote: Implementers MAY provide for some small leeway, usually no more than a few minutes, to account for clock skew.

claim: Every JWT must include an expiration time; a token without "exp" is not valid.
quote: The "exp" (expiration time) claim identifies the expiration time on or after which the JWT MUST NOT be accepted for processing.

claim: JWTs that carry personal data must be encrypted, not just signed.
quote: JWTs represent a set of claims as a JSON object that is encoded in a JWS and/or JWE structure.

claim: The "iat" claim requires validators to reject tokens whose issue time is in the future.
A parser that sees the same claim name twice must either reject the token or keep only the last value.
quote: JWT parsers MUST either reject JWTs with duplicate Claim Names or use a JSON parser that returns only the lexically last duplicate member name
